findings.behavior: SIGUSR1 closes producer admission, finishes accepted work, persists checkpoints and stops autonomous, maintenance and transport tasks. Drained process waits only for TERM/INT. No same-process resume exists; recovery requires a sanctioned retained-stage restart.

SIGTERM/INT closes admission, joins accepted workers, seals NEXT and exits. Existing launch hold blocks the replacement shell; it does not pause the current agent. The coordinator immediately releases its hold after verified drain and exposes no separate maintenance-window hold/resume CLI.
Existing wrappers require actor codex-astra-interactive; current codex-mlx-upgrade pause is rejected before signal. Ownership should be generalized explicitly, not impersonated.

build_bridge.sh --drain-only passes legacy target/release binary, whereas current process uses retained stage. Exact executable validation rejects it. Direct bridge_drain.py supports the actual staged binary, but drain still requires restart to resume.

limitations: Minime restart requires fresh relevant baseline.
Agent hold does not guarantee Ollama memory release or prevent other consumers from using Ollama.
Reduced-contention measurements do not establish ordinary-production performance.
Bridge drain also closes its transport tasks and cannot meet a restart-free requirement.
